A.biggest_strength: Comprehensive interactive coverage across 14 languages and architectures, paired with a rock-solid, linear 5-phase execution stepper that is instantly clear to newcomers.
A.biggest_weakness: The call stack visualization relies primarily on static text inside stacked boxes and badges ('text next to pictures') rather than visually demonstrating the mechanics of parameter binding and return value substitution.

B.biggest_strength: Exemplary visual mechanism where animated argument chips physically flow into parameter slots, return values rewrite paused caller expressions, and real bytecode/assembly listings reveal the underlying machine mechanism.
B.biggest_weakness: Interactive walkthrough is restricted to only 6 languages (the rest are in a static table), and the overlapping scene-versus-step navigation with an auto-tour creates slight interaction friction.

structured_output.reasons: Page B is the overall winner because it truly visualizes the mechanics of a function call rather than simply displaying text inside boxes. By animating argument tokens into parameter slots, showing expression substitution upon return, and providing real disassembled bytecode and empirical stack-limit benchmarks, B builds an unmatched mental model of how function calls work. While Page A offers broader interactive language coverage (14 vs. 6), its visuals are conventional static cards that don't capture the dynamism of execution.
